text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.2% today as oil prices climbed on geopolitical tensions—Brent crude jumped above $90 after U.S. strikes on Iranian targets, and the broader energy market is reacting to Russia's threats against Ukraine's energy infrastructure. Refinery utilization is running at 97.4%, near capacity, which means higher crude prices translate more directly into refiner margins and earnings; the company benefits when oil gets more expensive and refineries are already running hard.

The stock is also riding a broader rally in the refining sector tied to White House attention on boosters to refining capacity—the administration is meeting with refiners this week as gas prices become a political priority heading into midterms. That political momentum, combined with the tight refinery operating environment and rising crude costs, has pushed Marathon up 4.2% over the past two weeks.
